original_question: A pure f-vector is the rank vector of a pure simplicial complex, equivalently a pure O-sequence generated by squarefree monomials. What is the smallest number of variables n, equivalently the smallest number of vertices of the underlying simplicial complex, for which a nonunimodal pure f-vector can exist?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Open Problem 6: "What is the smallest number of variables n (i.e., the number of vertices of the complex) allowing the existence of a nonunimodal pure f-vector?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly identifies the object as a pure f-vector, correctly uses the paper's equivalence with pure O-sequences generated by squarefree monomials, and correctly asks for the minimum n interpreted both as the number of variables and as the number of vertices.
missing_details: The exact target is Section 5, Open Problem 6, not the neighboring problem about the smallest codimension for a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4.
The minimization is over all pure f-vectors; no socle degree, type, dimension, or Cohen-Macaulay hypothesis is fixed.
In the simplicial-complex formulation, a pure f-vector is the rank vector counting faces in each rank, beginning with 1 for the empty face.
Pure means that all facets of the simplicial complex have the same dimension; equivalently, in the algebraic formulation, all maximal squarefree monomial generators have the same degree.
In the equivalent algebraic formulation one works in K[y_1,...,y_n], but the existence question does not depend on the choice of the field K.
The question is existential and asks for the least integer n for which such an example exists.
Nonunimodal should be read against the paper's stated convention for unimodality: weakly increasing up to a peak and then weakly decreasing.
refined_question: What is the smallest integer n such that there exists a pure simplicial complex on n vertices whose rank vector (that is, its pure f-vector, counting faces in each rank and beginning with 1 for the empty face) is nonunimodal?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, what is the least n for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence arising from a pure monomial order ideal in K[y_1,...,y_n] whose maximal generators are squarefree monomials all of the same degree?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 5, Open Problem 6, where the paper asks verbatim for the smallest number of variables/vertices allowing a nonunimodal pure f-vector (Section 5, Open Problem 6, PDF pp. 16-17). Section 3 supplies the exact equivalence needed to make the question stand alone: pure f-vectors are the rank vectors of pure simplicial complexes and are precisely the pure O-sequences generated by squarefree monomials (Section 3, discussion preceding Example 3.1, PDF pp. 9-10). I did not redirect the question to the nearby but different unimodality problem for pure O-sequences of socle degree 4, because that is a separate question treated in Section 2 and listed separately again as Open Problem 4 (Section 2, Example 2.10 and Theorem 2.11, PDF pp. 5-6; Section 5, Open Problem 4, PDF p. 16). The only sharpening needed was to make explicit the quantifier "least n," the fact that no socle degree/type/dimension/Cohen-Macaulay restriction is imposed, and the field-independence of the equivalent algebraic formulation, all of which are implicit in the paper's definitions and local context (Section 2, definitions of pure O-sequence and field-independence, PDF p. 2).
